rationale: Base station storage was at 100% with loop recording disabled, triggering error E-402, which stops new event clips from being saved. The customer enabled Loop Recording and confirmed new events are now recording, resolving the issue. This is a standard L1 fix with no evidence of hacking or deleted recordings.

repair_steps: Confirm base station storage is no longer full and loop recording is enabled.
Verify new event clips are being saved successfully.
Clear error E-402 from the base station status.
Document the resolution in the case notes.
output.customer_reply: We're glad to hear that enabling Loop Recording resolved the issue and new events are now saving. Your base station will automatically overwrite the oldest clips when storage is full, so you won't need to manage storage manually. If you need any further assistance, feel free to reach out. Thank you for your patience!

args.query: E-402 storage full loop recording off fix procedure

args.action: Walk the customer through: open the app > Base Station Settings > Storage. First, if they want to keep any existing clips, export them. Then enable "Loop Recording" (this will overwrite oldest clips automatically). If they prefer a clean slate, format the storage instead. Confirm which option they chose and whether new events now record.

results.text: Base station storage at or above 98 percent with loop recording disabled. Frontline action: enable loop recording or format storage.

Event clips are stored on the base station's internal eMMC (HB-100: 16 GB, HB-200: 32 GB). When loop recording is disabled and storage reaches 98 percent, new events are not recorded and error E-402 is shown. Enable loop recording in Base Station Settings > Storage, or format the storage after exporting clips.

Solid blue: online and connected to cloud. Blinking blue: pairing mode (lasts 120 seconds). Solid red: no internet uplink. Blinking red: booting or firmware update in progress, do not unplug. Solid purple: storage almost full (over 95 percent).
